verses.zh: 我又看见一位天使从天降下，手里拿着无底坑的钥匙和一条大链子。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw an angel descending from heaven, holding[NOTE:2] in his hand the key to the abyss and a huge chain.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.

The two clauses “having/holding the key of the abyss” and “a huge chain in his hand” can be construed in two ways: (1) both are controlled by the participle ἔχοντα (echonta) and both are modified by the phrase “in his hand”—“having in his hand the key to the abyss and a huge chain.” (2) The participle ἔχοντα refers only to the key, and the phrase “in his hand” refers only to the chain—“having the key of the abyss and holding a huge chain in his hand.” Because of the stylistic tendency in Rev to use the verb ἔχω (echō) to mean “hold (something)” and the phrase “in his hand” forming a “bracket” along with the verb ἔχω around both the phrases in question, the first option is preferred.

verses.zh: 他捉住那龙，就是古蛇，又叫魔鬼，也叫撒但，把它捆绑一千年，
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] seized the dragon—the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan—and tied him up for a thousand years.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.

verses.zh: 扔在无底坑里，将无底坑关闭，用印封上，使它不得再迷惑列国。等到那一千年完了，以后必须暂时释放它。
verses.en: The angel[NOTE:1] then[NOTE:2] threw him into the abyss and locked[NOTE:3] and sealed it so that he could not deceive the nations until the one thousand years were finished. (After these things he must be released for a brief period of time.)
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (the angel introduced in v. 1) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.

Or “and shut.” While the lexical force of the term is closer to “shut,” it is acceptable to render the verb ἔκλεισεν (ekleisen) as “locked” here in view of the mention of the key in the previous verse.

verses.zh: 我又看见几个宝座，也有坐在上面的，并有审判的权柄赐给他们。我又看见那些因为给耶稣作见证，并为　神之道被斩者的灵魂，和那没有拜过兽与兽像，也没有在额上和手上受过他印记之人的灵魂，他们都复活了，与基督一同作王一千年。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw thrones and seated on them were those who had been given authority to judge.[NOTE:2] I also saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of the testimony about Jesus and because of the word of God. These[NOTE:3] had not worshiped the beast or his image and had refused to receive his mark on their forehead or hand. They[NOTE:4] came to life[NOTE:5] and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Grk “I saw thrones, and those seated on them, and judgment was given to them.” BDAG 567 s.v. κρίμα 3 says, “judging, judgment, the κρίμα ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς authority to judge was given to them Rv 20:4.”
Grk “God, and who.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation by supplying the pronoun “these” as subject.
Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
On the use of the aorist ἔζησαν (ezēsan) BDAG 425 s.v. ζάω 1.a.β says, “of dead persons who return to life become alive again: of humans in general (3 Km 17:23) Mt 9:18; Ac 9:41; 20:12; Rv 20:4, 5.”

verses.zh: 这是头一次的复活。（其余的死人还没有复活，直等那一千年完了。）
verses.en: (The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were finished.)[NOTE:1] This is the first resurrection.
notes: This statement appears to be a parenthetical comment by the author.

verses.zh: 在头一次复活有分的有福了，圣洁了！第二次的死在他们身上没有权柄。他们必作　神和基督的祭司，并要与基督一同作王一千年。
verses.en: Blessed and holy is the one who takes part[NOTE:1] in the first resurrection. The second death has no power over them,[NOTE:2] but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with him for a thousand years.
notes: Grk “who has a share.”

The shift from the singular pronoun (“the one”) to the plural (“them”) in the passage reflects the Greek text: The singular participle ὁ ἔχων (ho echōn) is followed by the plural pronoun τούτων (toutōn). In the interests of English style, this is obscured in most modern translations except the NASB.

verses.zh: 那一千年完了，撒但必从监牢里被释放，
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when the thousand years are finished, Satan will be released from his prison
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

verses.zh: 出来要迷惑地上四方（原文是角）的列国，就是歌革和玛各，叫他们聚集争战。他们的人数多如海沙。
verses.en: and will go out to deceive[NOTE:1] the nations at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog,[NOTE:2] to bring them together for the battle. They are as numerous as the grains of sand in the sea.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “mislead.”
The battle with Gog and Magog is described in the OT in Ezek 38:1-39:20.
Grk “of whom the number of them [is] like the sand of the sea” (an allusion to Isa 10:22).

verses.zh: 他们上来遍满了全地，围住圣徒的营与蒙爱的城，就有火从天降下，烧灭了他们。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] went up[NOTE:2] on the broad plain of the earth[NOTE:3] and encircled[NOTE:4] the camp[NOTE:5] of the saints and the beloved city, but[NOTE:6] fire came down from heaven and devoured them completely.[NOTE:7]
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The shift here to past tense reflects the Greek text.

On the phrase “broad plain of the earth” BDAG 823 s.v. πλάτος states, “τὸ πλάτος τῆς γῆς Rv 20:9 comes fr. the OT (Da 12:2 LXX. Cp. Hab 1:6; Sir 1:3), but the sense is not clear: breadth = the broad plain of the earth is perh. meant to provide room for the countless enemies of God vs. 8, but the ‘going up’ is better suited to Satan (vs. 7) who has recently been freed, and who comes up again fr. the abyss (vs. 3).” The referent here thus appears to be a plain large enough to accommodate the numberless hoards that have drawn up for battle against the Lord Christ and his saints.
Or “surrounded.”

On the term παρεμβολή (parembolē) BDAG 775 s.v. states, “Mostly used as a military t.t.…so always in our lit.…1. a (fortified) camp…ἡ παρεμβολὴ τῶν ἁγίων Rv 20:9 is also to be understood fr. the OT use of the word.”
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
See L&N 20.45 for the translation of κατεσθίω (katesthiō) as “to destroy utterly, to consume completely.”

verses.zh: 那迷惑他们的魔鬼被扔在硫磺的火湖里，就是兽和假先知所在的地方。他们必昼夜受痛苦，直到永永远远。
verses.en: And the devil who deceived[NOTE:1] them was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur,[NOTE:2] where the beast and the false prophet are[NOTE:3] too, and they will be tormented there day and night forever and ever.
notes: Or “misled.”
Traditionally, “brimstone.”

The verb in this clause is elided. In keeping with the previous past tenses some translations supply a past tense verb here (“were”), but in view of the future tense that follows (“they will be tormented”), a present tense verb was used to provide a transition from the previous past tense to the future tense that follows.

verses.zh: 我又看见一个白色的大宝座与坐在上面的；从他面前天地都逃避，再无可见之处了。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] I saw a large[NOTE:2] white throne and the one who was seated on it; the earth and the heaven[NOTE:3] fled[NOTE:4] from his presence, and no place was found for them.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.
Traditionally, “great,” but μέγας (megas) here refers to size rather than importance.

Or “and the sky.” The same Greek word means both “heaven” and “sky,” and context usually determines which is meant. In this apocalyptic scene, however, it is difficult to be sure what referent to assign the term.

Or “vanished.”sn The phrase the earth and the heaven fled from his presence can be understood (1) as visual imagery representing the fear of corruptible matter in the presence of God, but (2) it can also be understood more literally as the dissolution of the universe as we know it in preparation for the appearance of the new heaven and new earth (Rev 21:1).

verses.zh: 我又看见死了的人，无论大小，都站在宝座前。案卷展开了，并且另有一卷展开，就是生命册。死了的人都凭着这些案卷所记载的，照他们所行的受审判。
verses.en: And I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne. Then[NOTE:1] books were opened, and another book was opened—the book of life.[NOTE:2] So[NOTE:3] the dead were judged by what was written in the books, according to their deeds.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the vision.
Grk “another book was opened, which is of life.”
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of the books being opened.
Grk “from the things written in the books according to their works.”

verses.zh: 于是海交出其中的死人；死亡和阴间也交出其中的死人；他们都照各人所行的受审判。
verses.en: The[NOTE:1] sea gave up the dead that were in it, and Death[NOTE:2] and Hades gave up the dead that were in them, and each one was judged according to his deeds.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
Here Death is personified (cf. 1 Cor 15:55).

verses.zh: 死亡和阴间也被扔在火湖里；这火湖就是第二次的死。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence within the narrative.

verses.zh: 若有人名字没记在生命册上，他就被扔在火湖里。
verses.en: If[NOTE:1] anyone’s name[NOTE:2] was not found written in the book of life, that person[NOTE:3] was thrown into the lake of fire.
notes: Here καί (kai) has not been translated because of differences between Greek and English style.
The word “name” is not in the Greek text, but is implied.
Grk “he”; the pronoun has been intensified by translating as “that person.”
